title: Control Flow: IF/ELSE, WHILE, and BEGIN/END
description: Write procedural T-SQL using BEGIN/END blocks, conditional IF/ELSE logic, and WHILE loops with BREAK and CONTINUE.

data.text: Most SQL you write is declarative — you say *what* you want and SQL Server figures out *how* to get it. But sometimes you need procedural logic: make a decision, loop, or group statements into a block. That is what control flow statements are for.

A BEGIN...END block groups two or more statements into a single logical unit. Without it, only the first statement after an IF condition belongs to the branch. The block is required when you need multiple statements to execute together.

data.title: BEGIN...END grouping multiple statements

data.text: IF evaluates a boolean condition. When the condition is TRUE, the statements in the IF branch run. ELSE handles the FALSE case. You can chain multiple branches with ELSE IF.

data.title: IF...ELSE IF...ELSE chain
data.code:
IF @score >= 90
    PRINT 'Grade: A'
ELSE IF @score >= 80
    PRINT 'Grade: B'
ELSE IF @score >= 70
    PRINT 'Grade: C'
ELSE
    PRINT 'Grade: F';

data.title: Single vs. multiple statements
data.text: When an IF branch has only one statement and no BEGIN...END, you can omit the block. When it has two or more statements, you must use BEGIN...END.
CASE — conditional expression inside a query

While IF/ELSE controls statement flow, CASE lets you inject conditional logic *inside* a SELECT or WHERE clause. It comes in two forms: simple (compares one expression) and searched (evaluates multiple conditions).

data.title: Simple CASE
data.code:
SELECT product_name,
       list_price,
       CASE
           WHEN list_price > 3000 THEN 'Premium'
           WHEN list_price > 1000 THEN 'Mid-range'
           ELSE 'Budget'
       END AS price_tier
FROM   production.products;

data.text: WHILE repeats a block of statements as long as its condition is TRUE. It is the primary looping construct in T-SQL. Always include a way for the loop to terminate — otherwise it runs forever.

data.title: WHILE with a counter
BREAK stops the loop; CONTINUE skips to the next iteration
Beware infinite WHILE loops
data.text: If the loop variable is never incremented inside the WHILE block, you get an infinite loop. Always use SET or another update inside BEGIN...END to make progress toward the termination condition.
WAITFOR pauses execution for a specified duration or until a time. It is useful for rate-limiting, polling, or scheduled tasks inside stored procedures.

data.title: WAITFOR DELAY and WAITFOR TIME
Control flow essentials
points: BEGIN...END groups multiple statements under a single IF or WHILE branch
IF/ELSE IF/ELSE creates conditional branches; CASE injects conditions inside queries
WHILE loops repeat as long as the condition is TRUE — always ensure termination
BREAK exits a loop; CONTINUE skips to the next iteration and keeps going
WAITFOR pauses execution for a duration or until a time
